page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard1.4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the first-generation Standard family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration allocates 4 physical CPU cores with 2 threads per core, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs. System memory totals 28.0 GB of RAM, offering a memory density of 3.5 GB per vCPU.

Architecturally, the instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent filesystems and operating system volumes. Furthermore, VM.Standard1.4 contains no specialized hardware accelerators, operating with zero dedicated GPUs. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside virtual cloud network interfaces.

From a hardware lifecycle perspective, the Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor represents a legacy Haswell-era deployment. Dedicated vCPU scheduling ensures predictable computing capacity without noisy-neighbor contention. The balanced CPU-to-memory profile makes the instance viable for general cloud services, middleware, application backends, and moderate batch processing tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard1.4 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, paired with 28.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring cloud block volumes for data persistence. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external connectivity. With dedicated CPU allocation and a balanced memory-to-core configuration, VM.Standard1.4 is suitable for middle-tier application hosting, standard web servers, development environments, and moderate database workloads.
